title: Personal Checking: Returned Item Fee and Overdraft Protection Transfer Fee Levels
content:
Two further Personal Checking charges vary by tier: the fee for a check or ACH debit that comes back unpaid for insufficient funds, and the fee for each overdraft protection transfer pulled in from a linked savings account, together with a daily ceiling on how many transfer fees one account can be charged.

## Parameters

1. **Returned item fee (USD)** — the charge whenever a check or an ACH debit is sent back unpaid for want of funds.
2. **Overdraft protection transfer fee (USD)** — charged for each transfer that moves money in from the linked savings account.
3. **Transfer fees per business day** — the ceiling on how many of those transfer charges a single account can bear in one business day.

## Schedule by tier

| Tier | Returned item fee | Overdraft protection transfer fee | Transfer fees per business day |
|---|---|---|---|
| Access Checking | 0.00 | 0.00 | 0 |
| Student Checking | 0.00 | 0.00 | 0 |
| Everyday Checking | 35.00 | 10.00 | 1 |
| Interest Checking | 35.00 | 10.00 | 1 |
| Premier Checking | 35.00 | 0.00 | 0 |
| Private Client Checking | 0.00 | 0.00 | 0 |

## Notes drawn from the table

- Only Everyday Checking and Interest Checking price overdraft protection transfers, at 10.00 USD each, and on those tiers no more than one such fee lands on an account in a business day.
- A transfer fee recorded on a Premier Checking or Private Client Checking account at any figure other than 0.00, or on Everyday or Interest Checking at a figure other than 10.00, departs from this schedule.
- Hypothetical example: an Interest Checking account that receives three overdraft protection transfers on one business day is charged one transfer fee of 10.00 USD for that day.
